extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, assignees, and practitioners (attorneys/agents) interacting with the USPTO; USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on who qualifies as a 'small entity' for reduced U.S. patent fees, how to determine and assert entitlement, what transfers or licences affect status, and procedural/signature requirements for making and maintaining the assertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of small entity (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.27(a): A small entity means any party (person, small business concern, or nonprofit organization) under paragraphs (a)(1) through (a)(3) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific sub-definitions (person, small business concern, nonprofit organization) in the regulation to determine small entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person (37 CFR 1.27(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'person' means any inventor or other individual (e.g., an individual to whom an inventor has transferred some rights) who has not assigned, granted, conveyed, or licensed, and is under no obligation under contract or law to assign, grant, convey, or license, any rights in the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An inventor who has transferred some rights, or is under an obligation to transfer some rights, can still qualify if all parties who have had rights also qualify as small entities (person, small business concern, or nonprofit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business concern (37 CFR 1.27(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A business concern that (i) has not assigned, granted, conveyed, or licensed, and is under no obligation to assign/grant/convey/license rights in the invention to any party which would not qualify as a small entity; and (ii) meets the SBA size standards set forth in 13 CFR 121.801–121.805.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about size standards may be directed to the SBA Office of Size Standards. Both ownership/obligation and SBA size rules must be satisfied to claim small business status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit organization (37 CFR 1.27(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprofit organization that (i) has not assigned/conveyed/licensed, and is under no obligation to transfer, rights in the invention to any party that would not qualify as a small entity; and (ii) is either (A) a university or other institution of higher education (with specified accreditation/degree criteria), (B) an organization described in 26 U.S.C. 501(c)(3) and exempt under 501(a), (C) a nonprofit scientific/educational organization under a state statute (35 U.S.C. 201(i)), or (D) a foreign nonprofit that would qualify under (B) or (C) if located in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation adopts the 35 U.S.C. 201(i) concept of universities and incorporates 501(c)(3)/501(a) tax-exempt organizations and certain state-qualified nonprofits. Purely research/manufacturing/service organizations not meeting the listed criteria are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: License to a Federal agency (37 CFR 1.27(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A license to a Federal agency resulting from a rights determination under Executive Order 10096 does not constitute a license that prohibits claiming small entity status for persons; and for small business concerns and nonprofits, a license to a Federal agency resulting from a funding agreement pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 202(c)(4) does not constitute a license for purposes of disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licenses to the government under certain statutory/funding-agreement contexts are treated as not disqualifying; but other government-held rights or government organizations themselves do not qualify as nonprofits for fee reduction purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security interest (37 CFR 1.27(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A security interest does not involve an obligation to transfer rights in the invention for purposes of paragraphs (a)(1)–(a)(3) unless the security interest is defaulted upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting security (e.g., using an application or patent as loan collateral) does not currently disqualify small entity status; but if the loan is defaulted and rights transfer to a non-small entity, entitlement is lost and must be reported (see notification rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Location (international applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small entities may claim reduced fees regardless of the country in which they are located; there is no U.S.-only location restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same definitions apply to all applicants equally in accordance with the Paris Convention; foreign universities/nonprofits may qualify if they meet the enumerated equivalency criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights in the invention (U.S. rights only)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'rights in the invention' under 37 CFR 1.27 refer to rights in the United States (e.g., rights to exclude or import into the United States).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers of rights in foreign patents (e.g., Japanese patent rights) do not affect small entity status unless corresponding U.S. rights are transferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer/assignment to non-small entity disqualifies
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor, small business concern, or nonprofit assigns, grants, conveys, licenses, or becomes obligated to transfer any rights in the invention to any party that would not qualify as a small entity, then the original party no longer qualifies for small entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All rights in the invention must be owned by small entities for reduced fees to be proper; transferring rights to a non-small entity to exploit the reduced-fee status is impermissible (illustrative case: Ulead Systems v. Lex Computer & Management).

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning rights can restore eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If rights transferred to a non-small entity are later returned so that all rights are held by small entities, reduced fees may be claimed again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration of small entity ownership allows claiming reduced fees, but proper notification/assertion procedures must be followed when reclaiming status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'license' (includes implied and prototype orders)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'license' includes non-exclusive as well as exclusive licenses and royalty-free as well as royalty-generating licenses. Implied licenses to use and resell patented articles purchased from a small entity do not preclude claiming small entity status. An order to a firm to build a prototype for the applicant’s own use is not considered a license for these purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every transfer of rights or arrangement with a third party is treated as a disqualifying license; look to the substance (e.g., implied resale rights vs. actual transfer/licensing) and court precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of small entity status permits reduced fees (37 CFR 1.27(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A small entity who has properly asserted entitlement pursuant to paragraph (c) will be accorded small entity status in the particular application or patent, allowing payment of certain reduced patent fees under 35 U.S.C. 41(h)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishment is application/patent-specific; once established in that file, specified reduced fees are allowed per statute/regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion by writing (37 CFR 1.27(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Small entity status may be established by a written assertion of entitlement that (i) is clearly identifiable, (ii) is signed, and (iii) conveys the concept of entitlement to small entity status (no particular words required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A one-sentence statement or a checked box can suffice; the assertion may appear in any paper filed with the application. The assertion must be signed by an authorized signatory (see signature rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion by payment of exact small entity basic filing or national fee (37 CFR 1.27(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment, by any party, of the exact amount of one of the small entity basic filing fees set forth in §§ 1.16(a)–(e) or the small entity basic national fee in § 1.492(a) will be treated as a written assertion of entitlement to small entity status (even if the fee type was inadvertently selected in error).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of small entity basic filing/national fees in the exact amount is treated as an assertion; payment of other small-entity fees or incorrect amounts will not be treated as an assertion and are insufficient to establish status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign or file the written assertion (37 CFR 1.27(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The written assertion can be signed by (i) a party authorized under §1.33(b) (e.g., an attorney/agent), (ii) at least one individual identified as an inventor (even if an oath/declaration under §1.63 has not been submitted), or (iii) an assignee of an undivided part interest (subject to limitations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: one pro se inventor among three may submit the assertion; a partial assignee may sign but cannot file without recourse to an authorized party under §1.33(b) in some cases. Assignees asserting status are not required to submit a 3.73(b) certification in certain circumstances (see MPEP text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion in related, continuing, and reissue applications required (37 CFR 1.27(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Status as a small entity must be specifically established by an assertion in each related, continuing, and reissue application where status is appropriate and desired; status in one application does not affect any other application or patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refiling under §1.53 (continuation, divisional, CIP, or RCE) or filing a reissue requires a new assertion for the continuing/reissue application (RCE does not require a new assertion because it is not a new application).

rubrics_metrics.name: When small entity fees (other than basic filing/national) can be paid (37 CFR 1.27(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fee other than the small entity basic filing fees and the small entity national fees of paragraph (c)(3) can be paid in the small entity amount only if it is submitted with, or subsequent to, the submission of a written assertion of entitlement to small entity status (except when refunds are permitted by §1.28(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written assertion must precede or accompany payment of most reduced fees; mere payment of other smaller fees without prior assertion is not sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only one assertion required per application/patent; effect and duration (37 CFR 1.27(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: An assertion of small entity status need only be filed once in an application or patent. Small entity status, once established, remains in effect until changed pursuant to paragraph (g)(1). A second assertion is not required where rights are later divided among small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If small entity status is withdrawn, a new written assertion is required to regain status. Establishment persists through prosecution until issue or maintenance fee events trigger a new determination (see paragraph (g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of entitlement required before asserting (37 CFR 1.27(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to submitting an assertion of entitlement, a determination of such entitlement should be made pursuant to paragraph (a) to ensure that all parties holding rights in the invention qualify for small entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will generally not question an assertion made in accordance with the rules, but the applicant/practitioner should verify that all rights holders qualify; inaccurate assertions may have consequences (fraud provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: New determination and notification when issue/maintenance fees are due (37 CFR 1.27(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: (g)(1) Once established, small entity fees may be paid without regard to a change in status until the issue fee or any maintenance fee is due. (g)(2) Notification of loss of entitlement must be filed in the application or patent prior to paying, or at the time of paying, the earliest of the issue fee or any maintenance fee due after status is no longer appropriate. The notification must be signed by a party identified in §1.33(b). Payment of a fee in other than the small entity amount is not sufficient notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A change in ownership or rights that makes small entity status inappropriate must be reported before paying the relevant issue/maintenance fee; merely paying the larger fee does not substitute for the required signed notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud and improper establishment of small entity status (37 CFR 1.27(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attempt to fraudulently establish status as a small entity, or pay fees as a small entity, shall be considered a fraud practiced or attempted on the Office. Improperly and with intent to deceive establishing status or paying fees as a small entity is fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentional deception in asserting or using small entity status may result in fraud findings and associated sanctions; practitioners and parties must take reasonable care in determining and asserting entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assertion implies certification under 37 CFR 10.18(b) (signature and content certifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.4(d)(4) and 37 CFR 1.27, an assertion of entitlement to small entity status inherently contains a certification under 37 CFR 10.18(b): that statements of knowledge are true, statements on information/belief are believed true, and that the submitting party has made a reasonable inquiry supporting the paper (10.18(b) elements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making an assertion imports the professional/signature certification regime: misrepresentations can lead to sanctions under §10.18 and professional discipline for practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and signature-authenticity certifications (37 CFR 10.18(d)(4)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person submitting a document signed by another must have a reasonable basis to believe the signature was actually inserted by that person and should retain evidence of authenticity. Self-certification: the person inserting a signature certifies it is his/her own. Violations may lead to sanctions under §10.18(c)–(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure signatures are authentic and retained evidence of authenticity when filing assertions; improper signature handling can trigger sanctions and disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical form guidance and examiner notice (MPEP sample paragraph ¶5.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may notify applicants that the application may qualify for Small Entity Status and that the applicant must determine entitlement and submit a written assertion under 37 CFR 1.27(c) before fees can be paid in the small entity amount. No particular form is required for the written assertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A simple written assertion, check-box, or transmittal-sentence is sufficient; practitioners may still use older USPTO forms if educational for clients. The MPEP provides a sample examiner paragraph for notification.
